purpose: Initial future UI/gameplay concept boards; proposal, not shipped screens.

concepts.name: Tickle Duet
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: initial game-design concept board for Tickle the Pig, with UI mockups and an illustrated gameplay-feel vignette.
Create a polished landscape board, around 1536x1024 proportions, warm paper background, title across top, THREE clear columns: left a tall portrait mobile screen showing the match/lobby; middle a tall portrait mobile screen showing actual active gameplay; right a larger lively illustrated vignette expressing the physical play and emotion. Make the two mobile UIs legible, with generous large type, complete uncropped screen content, no phone hardware or device bezel. Each UI uses warm cream paper, thick dark-brown ink outlines, softly rounded paper stickers, pale sun-yellow primary button, muted sage/sky/rose fills, Caprasimo-like chunky friendly serif headings, Nunito-like rounded body lettering, handwritten small captions. Pigs are the round cartoon pigs in reference 1, especially Rosie (pink) and Copper (rust orange), preserving their huge dark eyes, oval snouts, small four-legged bodies, curly tails and black/brown outlines. Match the expressive 2D pig identity exactly rather than inventing generic pigs. Reference 2 is a mood/environment reference only; reference 3 shows existing paper UI and pig staging. Backgrounds are painterly farm pastures, red barns, daisies and bunting in the established palette. Pigs wear small owned-looking hats for identity only.
Lobby must show these two entry choices clearly: "Find a pig" and "Play with a friend". No five-mode selector. Game UI should make the player's role/gesture immediately visible; show player names "You" and "Clover", and an easy leave/back control. No paywall, currency entry fee, money prizes, chat box, guns, combat damage, neon HUD, glossy casino UI, hunger/happiness stat bars, or 3D humans. All labels are ordinary player-facing wording, never backend terms. Any progress meter is only for this minigame. Do not show existing Tickle bank currency as fuel for minigame gestures. These are future concept mockups, not screenshots.

Title (verbatim): "Tickle Duet". Subtitle: "Two pigs. One ridiculous giggle."
Lobby screen: paper title "Tickle Duet", Rosie and Copper sitting facing inward in a daisied barnyard, small line "2 pigs · about a minute", two buttons "Find a pig", "Play with a friend". Bottom caption "Make a little mischief together."
Active game screen: title "Tickle Duet", top simple shared minigame progress "Giggles 4 / 6"; player chips "You" and "Clover"; two large pigs facing one another, Copper wearing a straw hat. A warm paper cue over Rosie shows a two-icon sequence of gentle belly tickle and nose boop; caption "Clover's turn to copy". Two large reachable icon buttons at bottom "Tickle" and "Boop", plus a friendly "Ready?" nod cue. This is a slow playful call-and-response duet, not a frantic tapping race or exact beat rhythm game. Small caption "Copy your partner's silly pattern".
Right vignette: Rosie giggles leaning back while Copper gently boops her nose; a few playful feathers/heart-shaped giggle puffs and curved motion lines show the exchange; same pasture ground plane. Show delighted reciprocal play, not one pig attacking another. Below vignette put exactly "Listen. Copy. Giggle."

Title (verbatim): "Mud Volley". Subtitle: "A friendly splat across the fence."
Lobby screen: title "Mud Volley", Rosie and Copper on either side of a low pasture fence with a soft mud ball, line "2 pigs · five rallies", buttons "Find a pig", "Play with a friend".
Active game screen: title "Mud Volley", paper score strip "You 2 · Clover 1", label "Rally 4 / 5"; central illustrated side view of pink Rosie at bottom-left and Copper at upper-right across a low fence, a single soft mud ball with a dotted curved proposed throw trajectory and THREE broad landing zones marked with simple hoofprints. Gameplay is discrete, turn-based aim and response, no continuous action netcode. A large paper cue "Your toss!" and thumb control showing a short drag arrow plus caption "Drag to choose a spot"; one large confirm button "Toss". Opponent has a little ready pose. Keep score chip secondary to pigs, mud and gesture.
Right vignette: soft mud ball playfully splats beside Copper; both pigs grin, with a goofy mud moustache and floppy straw hat; sunny pasture and daisies. No injury. Below vignette put exactly "Aim. Toss. Splat."

Title (verbatim): "Truffle Trail". Subtitle: "One sniffs. One digs."
Lobby screen: title "Truffle Trail", Rosie sniffing and Copper holding a little wooden shovel beside a truffle basket, line "2 pigs · three hidden finds", buttons "Find a pig", "Play with a friend".
Active game screen: title "Truffle Trail", top shared round count "Basket 1 / 3"; player role chip "You · Digger" and partner chip "Clover · Sniffer". A tactile three-by-three illustrated mud tile board occupying most of the screen with one circled tile suggested by partner, pig faces at its edges. A paper partner clue "I smell it near the daisies!" with clear little daisy icon, not a free text chat field; caption "Clover marked a patch". Broad native-looking tap action cue "Pick a patch to dig" and yellow button "Dig here". Show role-specific information via a tiny inset paper "Sniffer's view": broad smell-strength ring on their own clue card, with hidden information not visible on the digger board. This is a standalone shared co-op puzzle; not the existing personal Truffle Patch or Sounder feeding.
Right vignette: Rosie noses a trail of scent curls while Copper flips a muddy tile to reveal a plump truffle; they fill one small basket together; wildflowers and red barn far off. Below vignette put exactly "Sniff. Point. Discover."

Title (verbatim): "Picnic Relay". Subtitle: "Make the world's messiest lunch."
Lobby screen: title "Picnic Relay", Rosie and Copper sitting at gingham picnic cloth with clover, apple slices and bowls, line "2 pigs · three silly recipes", buttons "Find a pig", "Play with a friend".
Active game screen: title "Picnic Relay", top shared progress "Lunches 1 / 3"; role chips "You · Picker" and "Clover · Mixer"; large simple illustrated recipe card "Clover crunch" with pictograms of two clover leaves and one apple slice, a clear ingredient tray of FOUR big tappable ingredients, and partner's big mixing bowl on the other half. Show one apple slice visually being sent toward partner via a soft curved arrow; cue "Pass the apple to Clover"; one yellow button "Pass it!" at bottom. Partner mixing action is represented by a paper checkmark/ready cue; player does not control both roles. This is forgiving cooperative sequence-and-handoff play rather than frantic overcooked timer pressure.
Right vignette: Rosie presents apple slices; Copper enthusiastically stirs, a harmless little clover leaf floats onto his snout, both laugh; a pair of finished bowls are shared equally. Below vignette put exactly "Pick. Pass. Stir."

Title (verbatim): "Pig Pageant". Subtitle: "A tiny runway for very big hats."
Lobby screen: title "Pig Pageant", Rosie, Copper and Pepper in silly temporary costumes on a little barn stage, line "3 pigs · one silly theme", buttons "Find a pig", "Play with a friend".
Active game screen: title "Pig Pageant", theme paper banner "Theme: Rainy-day royalty"; three player chips "You", "Clover", "Moss"; large Rosie preview wearing yellow rain boots and a leaf crown, with broad paper dresser tray showing a SHARED borrowed set of six playful costume props: umbrella, leaf crown, rain boots, tiny cape, flower bonnet, kettle hat. Caption "Everyone gets the same dress-up box". Three clear costume slots with current selections and one big yellow "Ready for the runway" button. Show a tiny stage vignette at bottom with the other two pigs in preview silhouettes. No expensive wardrobe gating, player-voted currency prizes, or beauty ratings.
Right vignette: all THREE distinct reference pigs parade under barn bunting on a tiny handmade stage in different funny rainy royalty costumes, with ribbon awards that each say a positive category such as "Best puddle strut" without a winner-takes-all podium. They cheer for each other. Below vignette put exactly "Dress. Strut. Cheer."
